evidence: Turner explicitly derives Phalura nihāṛa, Torwali niō, Punjabi/Lahnda neṛe, Hindi nīre and eastern niyar from nikaṭam. The addenda give Western Pahari neḍi and nɛṛu. These survey forms match the regional intervocalic-retroflex/flap series; Kullui lateral variants are included as comparative members of that local series, without proposing a separate sound law. Both Gujari slash variants belong to the same family.

Turner includes Gujarati nīcε, Oriya nice and Old Marwari nīcaï below in the nīca family, explaining the strengthened cc by influence of opposite ucca. The western Bhili survey s/ts variants and inflected final vowels match this below/low series. Multiword and -l/-ḍ-expanded responses are excluded here.

Turner explicitly gives Assamese/Bengali tale and Oriya taḷe as below postpositions/adverbs, beside tal/talā bottom. The Hajong tol- locative responses and Oriya tolo belong to that simple tala family; no extra directional noun is being ignored.

Turner gives Torwali dū, Phalura dhūro, Western Pahari dūr, Oriya dūra and eastern dur under dūra, including adverbial and adjectival case forms. These single-stem survey responses continue that regional family with locative/adverbial endings; Kullui lateral/vowel and aspirated variants remain explicitly comparative. Responses containing an additional adjective or adverb are excluded.
